Q.	Messier’s Catalogue was too small, as astronomical discoveries accelerated in the 19th century. John Dreyer made the next attempt at compiling a list of objects in the night sky and assigning them specific identifying numbers. Dreyer’s 1888 work is known by the three-letter acronym X. X contains 7,840 objects, including galaxies, star clusters and emission nebulae. Dreyer published two supplements to X in 1895 and 1908, known as the Index Catalogues (abbreviated IC), describing a further 5,386 astronomical objects. Thousands of these objects are best known by their X or IC numbers, which remain in widespread use. Our galactic neighbor Andromeda gets the number 224 in X. ID X.
